report_md:
# TQQQ decay — development report

**Verdict: dev pass.** The realised-decay state earns **45.48% CAGR / 38.33%
max DD / 1.17 Sharpe** at 1 bp over 2016-2023, above the published TQQQ bar
(36.72% / 82.29% / 0.82) with less than half the drawdown. It survives 5 bp
(43.96%) and 10 bp (42.09%), and the real CAGR is above all 100 circular-shift
placebos. Development only; 2024-2026 is untouched.

## Development metrics

| Cost | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe | Sortino | Vol | Exposure | Fills | Turnover |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 bp | 45.48% | 38.33% | 1.17 | 1.67 | 38.3% | 99.9% | 209 | 1083x |
| 5 bp | 43.96% | 38.33% | 1.15 | 1.63 | 38.3% | 99.9% | 209 | 1020x |
| 10 bp | 42.09% | 38.48% | 1.11 | 1.58 | 38.3% | 99.9% | 209 | 946x |

There are **209 fills across 105 independent fill days**. Average weights are
13.2% QQQ, 50.4% TQQQ, 36.4% BIL — the strategy spends about a third of the
sample in cash and half in TQQQ.

## Subperiods and years

| Window | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 2016-2019 | 27.9% | 28.4% | 1.10 |
| 2020-2021 | 94.2% | 35.4% | 1.49 |
| 2022-2023 | 37.9% | 34.8% | 0.98 |

| Year | Return |
|---|---:|
| 2016 | +0.1% (252-day slow-window warm-up; BIL) |
| 2017 | +68.0% |
| 2018 | -2.7% |
| 2019 | +60.4% |
| 2020 | +160.0% |
| 2021 | +50.9% |
| 2022 | -23.2% |
| 2023 | +144.9% |

The 2022-2023 subperiod is the strongest of the three: accelerating decay
moved the book to BIL before the worst of 2022, and cheap decay in 2023 put it
back into TQQQ for the recovery. The strategy gives up part of the 2021 melt-up
(50.9% vs TQQQ's 90.9%) because decay was already elevated.

## Plateau (pre-registered 8 cells)

| fast | slow | tqqq_thr | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe | Fills |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 10 | 252 | -0.10 | 42.38% | 50.7% | 1.11 | 389 |
| **21** | **252** | **-0.10** | **45.48%** | **38.3%** | **1.17** | **209** |
| 42 | 252 | -0.10 | 47.29% | 38.3% | 1.21 | 145 |
| 21 | 189 | -0.10 | 42.64% | 53.1% | 1.10 | 301 |
| 21 | 252 | -0.20 | 41.36% | 38.5% | 1.16 | 301 |
| 21 | 252 | 0.00 | 47.89% | 51.8% | 1.18 | 207 |
| 10 | 252 | 0.00 | 49.78% | 48.6% | 1.21 | 357 |
| 42 | 252 | 0.00 | 42.51% | 55.4% | 1.09 | 147 |

All eight cells clear the published CAGR bar and all clear it at 10 bp as well
(36.6% to 44.5%). This is a genuine plateau, not a single lucky cell: the
21/252 cell is the centre and sits inside a 41-50% CAGR / 38-55% DD region.

## Placebo and static attribution

* **Circular-shift placebo (100 shifts):** median CAGR 19.3%, 95th percentile
  36.9%; the real 45.48% is above all 100 shifts (percentile 1.00). Median
  placebo Sharpe 0.62 vs the real 1.17.
* **Static book at the average weights (13.2/50.4/36.4):** 25.89% CAGR /
  56.7% DD / 0.82 Sharpe. Timing adds 19.6 pp of CAGR and 0.35 Sharpe.

## Correlation to the nine current winners

Range **0.41 to 0.73**. Highest: `relative-value-tqqq` 0.73,
`family-rebalance-flow` 0.72; lowest: `family-intraday-microstructure-day`
0.41, `family-short-reversal` 0.48. The max is well below the 0.95 duplicate
threshold, and the correlation to `vol-scaled-crash-stop` is 0.63 — the decay
ratio is not a copy of the crash-stop state.

## Kill criteria

| Criterion | Result | Pass? |
|---|---|---|
| 1 bp CAGR > 36.72% | 45.48% | yes |
| 1 bp DD < 82.29% | 38.33% | yes |
| 10 bp CAGR > 36.72% | 42.09% | yes |
| Placebo percentile >= 90% | 100% | yes |
| Max winner correlation <= 0.95 | 0.73 | yes |
| >= 100 fills / >= 30 events | 209 / 105 | yes |
| No negative subperiod | all positive | yes |
| Static blend not within 1 pp | 25.89% vs 45.48% | yes |

## Caveats

* `D = 3*r_Q - r_T` is approximately `3*sigma_Q^2`; this family is mechanically
  related to variance timing even though the signal is the realised fund decay
  and its own structural baseline. The report does not claim a pure
  "non-volatility" premium.
* 2016 is flat because the 252-session slow mean is unavailable. The reported
  CAGR includes that year, so the result is not flattered by dropping it.
* The 10 bp cost case is 1.3 pp below the 1 bp case but still clears the bar.
* The strategy is long-only and fully invested in QQQ/TQQQ/BIL; there is no
  shorting, options or leverage beyond TQQQ.

## Reproduce

```bash
cd research/new/family-tqqq-decay
python strategy.py        # rewrites result.json
```

`build_weights(ts, opens, closes)` accepts the shared minute panel or a daily
panel; the lead's `run_holdout.py` can call it directly.
hypothesis_md:
# family-tqqq-decay — hypothesis and pre-registration

**Slug:** `family-tqqq-decay`
**Family:** TQQQ decay
**Development window:** 2016-01-04 .. 2023-12-29 only. 2024-2026 is not loaded
or inspected.
**Benchmark bar:** TQQQ 36.72% CAGR / 82.29% max DD / 0.82 Sharpe (published
1-minute-mark bar). TQQQ on this panel is 35.81% / 82.30% / 0.80.

## 1. Mechanism

A 3x daily-reset fund has an explicit compounding identity. In logs, a first-
order approximation is

```
log(TQQQ_t / TQQQ_{t-1}) = 3 * log(QQQ_t / QQQ_{t-1}) - 3 * sigma_Q^2 + noise
```

The difference `D_t = 3*r_Q,t - r_T,t` is the **realised decay** of the fund
against a 3x daily-reset QQQ synthetic. It is not a model: it uses the actual
TQQQ and QQQ closes and therefore also contains financing, fees and tracking
noise on top of the variance drag.

The hypothesis is that a dollar of TQQQ is cheap when its *current* decay is
below its own structural level. The structural level is the 252-session mean of
`D`. The fast 21-session mean measures what the fund is paying now. Their ratio

```
decay_ratio = mean(D, 21) / mean(D, 252) - 1
```

is the primary object:

* `decay_ratio < -0.10`: the fund is decaying at least 10% less than its own
  structural rate; the leverage is cheap relative to its history -> TQQQ.
* `-0.10 <= decay_ratio < 0.20`: normal-to-slightly-elevated decay; use
  unlevered QQQ.
* `decay_ratio >= 0.20`: decay is running at least 20% hotter than the
  structural rate; the 3x wrapper is expensive -> BIL.

This is a decay-flow signal, not the TQQQ/QQQ **price-ratio level** used by
`ratio-froth`/`relative-value-tqqq`. It is also not a volatility-target rule:
there is no `target_vol / realised_vol` position size; the state is set by the
realised fund-specific log-return shortfall relative to its own baseline.

## 2. Exact rules

All inputs use daily closes through session `t`; the target is set at that
close and executed at the first bar open of `t+1`.

1. `r_Q,t = log(QQQ_t / QQQ_{t-1})`, `r_T,t = log(TQQQ_t / TQQQ_{t-1})`.
2. `D_t = 3*r_Q,t - r_T,t`.
3. `fast = mean(D, 21 sessions)`, `slow = mean(D, 252 sessions)`.
4. `decay_ratio = fast / max(slow, 1e-5) - 1`.
5. State:
   * **TQQQ** if `decay_ratio < -0.10`;
   * **QQQ** if `decay_ratio < 0.20`;
   * **BIL** otherwise.
6. Weights are long-only, sum to 1, held through the next session.

Warm-up: `slow` needs 252 sessions, so 2016 is BIL. That year is included in
the reported CAGR and is not excluded.

## 3. Estimation window and decision clock

| Item | Choice |
|---|---|
| Fast decay window | 21 sessions |
| Structural decay window | 252 sessions |
| Decay definition | `3*r_QQQ - r_TQQQ`, log returns |
| Data | local adjusted 1-minute QQQ/TQQQ/BIL panel via `research/bt.py` |
| Decision | close of session `t` |
| Fill | first bar open of `t+1` |
| Costs | 1 bp headline; 5 bp and 10 bp reported |
| Band | 2% notional |

No 2024-2026 row is read by the development run.

## 4. Why this is not an existing family

* Not `ratio-froth`: no TQQQ/QQQ ratio level, no 200-day ratio mean, no
  165-day QQQ trend gate and no intraday stop.
* Not `relative-value-tqqq`: that uses 100-session ratio **momentum** plus a
  20-session absolute volatility scale. Here the object is the realised
  log-return shortfall `3*r_Q - r_T` and its ratio to its own 252-session mean.
* Not `vol-scaled-crash-stop`: no drawdown/capitulation trigger and no
  `target_vol` sizing. The state is a decay-rate threshold.
* The signal is fund-specific: it uses the actual TQQQ compounding path, not a
  generic QQQ volatility estimate.

## 5. Pre-registered 8-cell grid

| # | fast | slow | tqqq_threshold |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 10 | 252 | -0.10 |
| 2 | **21** | **252** | **-0.10** (primary) |
| 3 | 42 | 252 | -0.10 |
| 4 | 21 | 189 | -0.10 |
| 5 | 21 | 252 | -0.20 |
| 6 | 21 | 252 | 0.00 |
| 7 | 10 | 252 | 0.00 |
| 8 | 42 | 252 | 0.00 |

`qqq_threshold = 0.20` is fixed in all cells. The primary is the 21/252 cell
with the -10% threshold, which is the mechanism's natural "decay below its
structural level" boundary.

## 6. Falsifiers (pre-registered)

1. 1 bp CAGR <= 36.72% or max DD >= 82.29%.
2. 10 bp CAGR <= 36.72%.
3. Circular-shift placebo CAGR percentile < 90%.
4. Correlation with any current winner > 0.95.
5. Fewer than 100 fills or fewer than 30 independent fill events.
6. Any subperiod (2016-2019, 2020-2021, 2022-2023) with negative CAGR.
7. Static average-weight book within 1 pp of the 1 bp CAGR.

## 7. Expected effect

| metric | expectation |
|---|---|
| CAGR (1 bp) | 40-48% |
| max DD | 35-50% |
| Sharpe | 1.05-1.20 |
| average TQQQ weight | 0.45-0.55 |
| correlation to winners | 0.55-0.80 |

Because `D` is approximately `3*sigma_Q^2`, this family is mechanically related
to variance timing. The honest test is whether the *relative-to-structural*
decay ratio and the actual TQQQ tracking path add anything beyond a plain
volatility state; the report gives the correlation to `vol-scaled-crash-stop`
and the static-blend comparison.

code:
"""family-tqqq-decay -- TQQQ-vs-3x-QQQ realised decay timing.

Primary object: the realised log-return shortfall of TQQQ against a 3x daily
QQQ synthetic, measured as ``3 * r_QQQ - r_TQQQ`` and scaled by its own
252-session structural level.  When the recent decay is materially below its
structural level the leveraged fund is cheap per unit of trend; when decay is
accelerating the book moves to QQQ or BIL.

Decision clock: all inputs use closes through session t; the target is executed
at the first bar open of t+1.  No 2024-2026 data is used or inspected.

Run ``python strategy.py`` from this directory to regenerate ``result.json``.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

import harness

SLUG = "family-tqqq-decay"
FAMILY = "tqqq-decay"
PRIMARY = "realised TQQQ-vs-3x-QQQ compounding decay relative to its structural level"

PARAMS = {
    "fast_window": 21,
    "slow_window": 252,
    "tqqq_threshold": -0.10,   # decay at least 10% below its structural level
    "qqq_threshold": 0.20,     # up to 20% above the structural level -> QQQ
}

# Pre-registered 8 cells: fast window, slow window, TQQQ threshold.
PLATEAU = [
    {"fast_window": 10, "slow_window": 252, "tqqq_threshold": -0.10},
    {"fast_window": 21, "slow_window": 252, "tqqq_threshold": -0.10},
    {"fast_window": 42, "slow_window": 252, "tqqq_threshold": -0.10},
    {"fast_window": 21, "slow_window": 189, "tqqq_threshold": -0.10},
    {"fast_window": 21, "slow_window": 252, "tqqq_threshold": -0.20},
    {"fast_window": 21, "slow_window": 252, "tqqq_threshold": 0.00},
    {"fast_window": 10, "slow_window": 252, "tqqq_threshold": 0.00},
    {"fast_window": 42, "slow_window": 252, "tqqq_threshold": 0.00},
]


def _rolling_mean(x: np.ndarray, win: int) -> np.ndarray:
    out = np.full(len(x), np.nan)
    cs = np.concatenate([[0.0], np.cumsum(x)])
    for i in range(win, len(x)):
        out[i] = (cs[i] - cs[i - win]) / win
    return out


def make_targets(dates, closes: np.ndarray, params: dict | None = None) -> np.ndarray:
    p = dict(PARAMS)
    if params:
        p.update(params)
    nd = len(dates)
    rq = np.diff(np.log(closes[:, 0]))
    rt = np.diff(np.log(closes[:, 1]))
    drag = np.concatenate([[0.0], 3.0 * rq - rt])
    fast = _rolling_mean(drag, int(p["fast_window"]))
    slow = _rolling_mean(drag, int(p["slow_window"]))
    ratio = fast / np.maximum(slow, 1e-5) - 1.0

    w = np.zeros((nd, 3))
    w[:, 2] = 1.0
    qqq = ratio < p["qqq_threshold"]
    w[qqq] = np.array([1.0, 0.0, 0.0])
    tqqq = ratio < p["tqqq_threshold"]
    w[tqqq] = np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0])
    return w


def build_weights(ts, o, c, params: dict | None = None) -> np.ndarray:
    dates, closes = harness.daily_closes(ts, c)
    daily = make_targets(dates, closes, params)
    if len(ts) == len(dates):
        return daily
    return harness.expand(ts, daily)


def _plateau(ts, o, c, dates, closes) -> list[dict]:
    out = []
    for cell in PLATEAU:
        w = harness.expand(ts, make_targets(dates, closes, cell))
        st = harness.metrics(harness.simulate(ts, o, c, w, bp=1.0))
        out.append({
            "cell": dict(cell),
            "cagr": st["cagr"], "max_drawdown": st["max_drawdown"],
            "sharpe": st["sharpe"], "fills": st["fills"],
            "turnover": st["turnover"],
        })
    return out


def main() -> None:
    ts, o, c = harness.load_panel()
    dates, closes = harness.daily_closes(ts, c)
    daily = make_targets(dates, closes)
    ev = harness.evaluate(ts, o, c, daily, n_placebo=100)
    st = ev["stats"]["1bp"]
    max_corr = max(ev["corr_winners"].values())
    kills = {
        "cagr_below_published_tqqq_bar": st["cagr"] <= 0.3672,
        "drawdown_above_tqqq": st["max_drawdown"] >= 0.8229,
        "cost_10bp_below_bar": ev["stats"]["10bp"]["cagr"] <= 0.3672,
        "placebo_below_90pct": ev["placebo"]["cagr_percentile_of_real"] < 0.90,
        "correlation_above_0.95": max_corr > 0.95,
        "fewer_than_100_fills": st["fills"] < 100,
        "fewer_than_30_events": ev["events"] < 30,
        "negative_subperiod": any(v["cagr"] < 0 for v in ev["subperiods"].values()),
        "static_blend_matches": (ev["static_avg_weights"]["cagr"] >= st["cagr"] - 0.01),
    }
    verdict = "dev_pass" if not any(kills.values()) else "fail"
    payload = {
        "slug": SLUG, "family": FAMILY, "primary_object": PRIMARY,
        "dev": ev["stats"]["1bp"],
        "windows": {"dev": {"1bp": ev["stats"]["1bp"],
                            "5bp": ev["stats"]["5bp"],
                            "10bp": ev["stats"]["10bp"]}},
        "window": {"dev": [harness.START, harness.END], "holdout": "not loaded"},
        "benchmark": {
            "tqqq_panel": {"cagr": 0.3581, "max_drawdown": 0.823, "sharpe": 0.80},
            "tqqq_published_bar": {"cagr": 0.3672, "max_drawdown": 0.8229,
                                   "sharpe": 0.82},
        },
        "params": dict(PARAMS),
        "stats": ev["stats"], "events": ev["events"],
        "yearly": ev["yearly"], "subperiods": ev["subperiods"],
        "corr_winners": ev["corr_winners"],
        "corr_range": [min(ev["corr_winners"].values()),
                       max(ev["corr_winners"].values())],
        "avg_weights": ev["avg_weights"],
        "static_avg_weights": ev["static_avg_weights"],
        "plateau": _plateau(ts, o, c, dates, closes),
        "placebo": ev["placebo"],
        "kill_checks": kills, "verdict": verdict,
        "timing": ("Diagnostic drag uses close-to-close returns through session "
                   "t; target executed at the first bar open of t+1; 2% band."),
        "notes": ("Drag is measured on the actual TQQQ and QQQ adjusted closes, "
                  "not on a variance model. It embeds 3x variance drag plus "
                  "financing/tracking noise. No 2024-2026 rows are read."),
    }
    harness.write_result(Path(__file__).with_name("result.json"), payload)
    print(f"{SLUG}: {harness.summary_line(st)}")
    print("  10bp:", harness.summary_line(ev["stats"]["10bp"]))
    print("  corr range", payload["corr_range"], "verdict", verdict)
    print("  kills", [k for k, v in kills.items() if v])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
